Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
All congruences are modulo \(397\). Since \(397\) is prime, every nonzero residue is invertible.

Because \(a_{2026}=9\neq 0\), none of \(a_0,a_1,\dots,a_{2026}\) can be \(0\); otherwise the recurrence would force all later terms to be \(0\). Also,

\[
a_{2027}(a_{2026}+1)^2=a_{2027}\cdot 10^2\equiv 9,
\]

so \(a_{2027}\neq 0\) as well. Define

\[
b_n=a_n^{-1}.
\]

From

\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2\equiv a_n
\]

and multiplying by \(a_n^{-1}a_{n+1}^{-1}\), we get

\[
\frac{(a_n+1)^2}{a_n}\equiv a_{n+1}^{-1}=b_{n+1}.
\]

But

\[
\frac{(a_n+1)^2}{a_n}=a_n+2+a_n^{-1}=a_n+2+b_n.
\]

Thus

\[
b_{n+1}=b_n+2+a_n,
\]

so

\[
a_n=b_{n+1}-b_n-2.
\]

Therefore

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
= \sum_{n=0}^{2026}(b_{n+1}-b_n-2)
= b_{2027}-b_0-2\cdot 2027.
\]

Since \(a_0=1\), we have \(b_0=1\). Also,

\[
b_{2027}=\frac{(a_{2026}+1)^2}{a_{2026}}
=\frac{10^2}{9}
=\frac{100}{9}.
\]

Hence the sum is congruent to

\[
\frac{100}{9}-1-4054
=
\frac{100}{9}-4055.
\]

Now compute modulo \(397\). Since \(9\cdot 44=396\equiv -1\), we have

\[
9^{-1}\equiv -44.
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{100}{9}=11+\frac1{9}\equiv 11-44=-33\equiv 364.
\]

Also,

\[
4055\equiv 85 \pmod{397}.
\]

So the sum is congruent to

\[
364-85=279.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
